Team / Alice —

I ran the numbers off Marissa’s suggested front-loading scenario and modeled both a 24m blended and a 36m prepay. Summary below; full file attached (Financial_Model_Cyclone_Options.csv).

Option A — 24m blended (accelerated Year1 pulse):
- Effective blended discount: ~12% across committed volumes (assumes financing cost of 3.5% annually).
- Cash profile: two payments in Year1 permitted (Day 0 and Day 180).
- NPV vs 36m prepay: ~+3% cost (i.e., Cyclone pays 3% more NPV vs 3yr full prepay).

Option B — 36m prepay (original slab-based pulses):
- Effective blended discount: ~18% across committed volumes (higher due to extended term and lower financing load).
- Cash profile: single upfront or annual prepay options.
- Additional: we can add a 1% grandfathering credit if Cyclone moves to a higher slab within Year2 (protects you if usage grows faster).

SLA credits question: for the onboarding SLO bump to 99.95% for first 6 months, we can provide a scaled credit schedule. Practical approach: cap credits at 10% of monthly invoice and apply prorated credits tied to outage minutes only when the issue is attributable to Redwood’s Dedicated runtime (excludes customer misconfigurations). I can draft the exact formula for legal.

Recommendation: If cash preferences push Cyclone to 24m, offer Option A with the two-payment Year1 plan and a 2% acceleration surcharge (applied only to Year1 effective rate). If they want the best blended unit economics, move to Option B.
